title: Structure Is All You Need to Reuse: Accelerating GraphRAG via Meta-Structure-Aware KV Caching

problem.claim: GraphRAG systems repeatedly encode structural logic in long textual prompts, causing prefilling latency, memory overhead, and limited cache reuse under entity-level variation.

gap.claim: Existing GraphRAG systems do not explicitly separate recurring graph structure from query-specific entity semantics for reusable KV caching.

contributions.claim: MetaKV decouples static structural logic from dynamic entity semantics in GraphRAG inference.
MetaKV mines frequent meta-structures and pre-computes reusable Skeleton KVs, then injects query-specific entity representations into reserved structural slots.
MetaKV introduces a Topological Mask that constrains attention to valid graph edges.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on HotpotQA and MetaQA report up to 6.4× prefilling speedup.
The authors report a 73% effective cache-hit rate.
The authors report competitive reasoning accuracy while maintaining adherence to graph topology.

narrative_sequence.summary: GraphRAG augments LLMs with structured, multi-hop evidence from knowledge graphs.
Textual linearization forces repeated schema-level reasoning and leads to latency, memory, and cache-reuse limitations.
Retrieved entities vary, but their logical meta-structures recur frequently, making structural encoding a repeated computational cost.
MetaKV reuses precomputed structural KV caches, injects dynamic entity representations, and constrains attention with a topological mask.
Experiments report speedup, cache-hit rate, and competitive reasoning accuracy on two datasets.

source_observation.claim: Logical graph schemas recur across queries even when retrieved entities differ.

interpretation.claim: Caching invariant structural computation may reduce repeated inference work under changing entity content.

application.claim: For structured retrieval systems, separate reusable structural representations from query-specific semantic representations when their recurrence is observable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that structural reuse is beneficial when schemas do not recur or when dynamic semantics alter the required topology.

source_observation.claim: A topological attention mask is used to constrain reasoning to valid graph edges.

interpretation.claim: Structural constraints can be incorporated into attention to support adherence to graph topology.

application.claim: When graph validity is important, constrain model attention using the known relation structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the mask's computational cost, coverage of graph errors, or behavior on incomplete graphs.

unknowns: Baseline systems and experimental protocol are not specified.
Exact reasoning-accuracy results and trade-offs are not reported.
The abstract does not quantify memory overhead or cache construction cost.
Generalization beyond HotpotQA and MetaQA is unknown.
